transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-19
Start time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Malhotra (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (CTO - Cardinal HealthTech), Samir Khan (Lead ML Eng), Tina Park (Product)

Auto-summary: quick sync focused on selecting a primary model to pin for the pilot, discussion about safe rollback gates, and additional benchmarking needs. Action items assigned.

Topics covered: model catalog comparison, pin strategy, fallback variants, emergency cutover criteria, KMS & retention, next benchmark runs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Alright hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — where we landed on model candidates after last week's tests, confirm pin rules for the pilot, and then agree next steps for rollback tabletop. can we go quick intros? 
[00:12] Marta Ruiz: Marta here, CTO. short on time today, want clear risk mitigations, especially on sensitive PHI-ish example traffic. 
[00:20] Samir Khan: Samir (Lead ML). ran the runs we discussed, have the logs but need help interpreting quantized outputs.
[00:28] Jordan Lee: Great. Priya from my side will walk through the observed latencies — she did the core bench runs. Priya, over to you. 
[00:35] Priya Malhotra: thanks. so quick primer: we tested three catalog candidates — LLM-XL-v2 (float16), LLM-XL-q4 (int8-ish quant), and LLM-Mid-2 (smaller) — across your sample prompt set. attached spreadsheet: /shared/benchmarks/cardinal-2026-11-18.csv. the headline: median latency at 256 tokens was 110ms for v2, 80ms for q4, and 45ms for mid-2. cost-per-token drops accordingly but quality delta for questions with long context increased on q4 vs v2 in ~12% of queries.
[01:10] Samir Khan: when you say quality delta, is that model hallucination or diminished instruction following? 
[01:14] Priya Malhotra: mostly instruction fidelity — a few completion truncation and context-merge errors. hallucinations were rare but present in q4 for long multi-step prompts. 
[01:25] Marta Ruiz: that's the worry; those are our high-risk flows. we need a pinned model that reduces that class of failure. 
[01:31] Jordan Lee: understood. one middle-ground we proposed is have LLM-XL-v2 as primary pinned model with q4 as fast fallback for non-sensitive routes. pin policy could be: primary pinned to v2 for routes with PII sensitivity flag, fallback to q4 for low-sensitivity or when latency breach occurs. 
[01:50] Tina Park: what about cost? if we keep v2 for all routes costs go up significantly. 
[01:54] Jordan Lee: yes total cost uplift estimated at ~2.3x if everything is on v2. that's why we want per-route pinning and smart routing; we can flag sensitive endpoints in the app to target the primary. 
[02:05] Priya Malhotra: also we can use prefix/KV caching for repeated context which reduces token work. note: some of the transcripts mention 'KV cash' in the logs — it's actually KV cache, sorry the ASR cut it. 
[02:16] Samir Khan: for the fallback, how do we avoid bad outputs when the system switches? I'm worried about sudden degradation mid-session. 
[02:22] Priya Malhotra: good call. recommended pattern is session sticky routing plus token-level downgrade with a short grace—when fallback triggers we keep session pinned for N requests (e.g., 3) and issue a rerank pass for the top-3 generated candidates. also we use soft-fallback: try q4 but if rerank score below threshold, automatically escalate to v2 via emergency retry. 
[02:47] Jordan Lee: those are the escape hatches. I want to call out rollbacks: we recommend a canary -> ramp plan with a deadman's switch. specific triggers: SLO breach (p95 latency > 500ms), error rate above X, or quality regression detected on the continuous eval set. if any trigger fires, automatic rollback to previous stable model version. 
[03:05] Marta Ruiz: who runs the deadman's switch? our infra team or Redwood console? 
[03:09] Jordan Lee: Redwood console can orchestrate the rollback — we expose an API and a manual 'execute rollback' button in the UI. for Dedicated/Private installs you can also control it locally. we will provide runbook steps for three modes: automated rollback, manual approve rollback, and emergency cutover. 
[03:26] Samir Khan: can you clarify what data we send to Redwood in hosted mode? we have to keep PII in-house. 
[03:31] Jordan Lee: yes, agreed. for Hosted we'll talk about redaction patterns; for anything regulated we strongly suggest Redwood Private (VPC) where data plane stays in your VPC. KMS/HSM integration is available and audit logs retained for 90 days by default — we can adjust retention on Dedicated.
[03:47] Tina Park: do you have SOC 2/ISO docs? procurement asked. 
[03:50] Jordan Lee: yes I'll send the security packet after the call. it's in our share link, but I'll push the KMS specifics as well. 
[03:57] Priya Malhotra: back to model pinning: Samir, you asked about soft revert — we can use request-level tagging so developers can see when a fallback occurred. those events are logged with token-level cost and model id. that'll help triage.
[04:12] Samir Khan: good. now on quantized models — we've seen some noise in logits with beam-style searches. is there guidance on temperature or decoding for q4? 
[04:20] Priya Malhotra: for q4 we recommend slightly lower temperature (0.6 vs 0.8 default) and increase top-p to 0.95 for question-answer flows. in rerank flows keep deterministic decoding where possible. we'll include the knob recommendations in the doc. 
[04:36] Jordan Lee: another item is rollout velocity — propose canary at 3% for 24h, ramp to 25% for 48h with metrics check, then full ramp. during canary, we run automated evals plus a human sample audit. if regression flagged, execute rollback.
[04:58] Marta Ruiz: what's the human audit cadence? our compliance wants a 24h turnaround for high-severity regressions. 
[05:03] Priya Malhotra: we can run the human-in-the-loop audit within 12-24 hours for canary samples if you share reviewers. Redwood can provide tooling to annotate and mark severity.
[05:14] Samir Khan: for the immediate pilot, can we pin v2 to the 3 critical routes and put q4 behind a feature flag for other low-priority routes? 
[05:21] Jordan Lee: yes that's exactly the plan. we'll supply the pin config JSON and a short example webhook for toggling. Samir, you'll get the config. 
[05:28] Samir Khan: excellent.
[05:30] Tina Park: one last security question — if we do Dedicated, does Redwood store audit logs outside our tenancy? 
[05:36] Jordan Lee: on Dedicated, logs can be exported to your S3 or SIEM; we do not retain user payloads by default. we'll include that in the checklist doc. 
[05:45] Priya Malhotra: circling back to the bench request — I ran a 2-hour tail-latency sweep; we saw sporadic spikes on q4 at 99.9th percentile when sequence length crossed ~4k tokens. attached plot: latency_histogram_99p.png. recommendation: do 4k+ seeds to stress test the long-tail. 
[06:08] Samir Khan: we do have flows that hit 6k tokens in rare batch ingest. can Redwood run a 6k stress? 
[06:13] Priya Malhotra: yes, we'll run that in the Dedicated sandbox, but it needs more GPU memory; for Hosted we can simulate but dedicated gives realistic tails. I'll queue a 6k run as an action item.
[06:25] Jordan Lee: ok let's capture next steps — Jordan to send pricing and security pack, Priya to run 6k stress and rerank quantized run, Samir to share canonical prompts. also schedule rollback tabletop on 2026-11-24 11:00 PST — does that work? 
[06:39] Marta Ruiz: that time works. please keep it tight — want tabletop <= 60 minutes. 
[06:44] Tina Park: please include product and legal for the tabletop. 
[06:47] Jordan Lee: will do. any other blockers? 
[06:50] Samir Khan: one more — can Redwood share sample logs format for the auto-detect triggers? the schema helps our infra build monitors. 
[06:56] Priya Malhotra: yes, we'll send an example webhook payload and the metric thresholds. note: schema uses 'model_id', 'request_id', 'latency_ms', 'fallback_triggered' fields. 
[07:07] Jordan Lee: perfect. quick recap: Primary recommendation: pin LLM-XL-v2 for sensitive routes, q4 as controlled fallback for latency-sensitive low-risk routes. Canary + ramp + deadman's switch + rerank guardrails. Action items and dates as called out.
[07:23] Marta Ruiz: good, appreciate the clarity. looking forward to the benchmark CSV and the deck for the tabletop.
[07:29] Jordan Lee: thanks all. we'll follow up with artifacts and meeting invite. 
[41:30] call ended
